name: City Council Workshop
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO CITY COUNCIL
  MEETING MINUTES
  Housing Workshop

  February 24, 2009

An Adjourned Meeting (Housing Workshop) of the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo,
California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 6:01 p.m., on February 24, 2009, at 200 Civic
Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 13, 2009, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

ROLL CALL

Present:  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem MacLean

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin Bornstein, Asst. City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Chuck Wilson, Director of Community Development
  Elaine Lister, Planning Manger
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ledesma

INVOCATION: Mayor Ury

City Council Minutes  1  February 24, 2009
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Gail Reavis, M.V.: stated that it is difficult to speak about matters that have been discussed
in closed session and it is not her intent to disclose anything confidential. She noted that
the State recertified the City’s Housing Element in 2007 and we are in compliance at this
time.

Roseanne Kotver, Community Activist, Laguna Niguel: stated that she is astounded by
fear-based arguments when affordable housing is being promoted; cities must respond to
the needs of their citizens and we must house people. She expressed support for Mission
Viejo’s efforts to put forward the opportunity for more housing particularly for those who
have low and very low income ranges.

Cesar Covarrubias, Kennedy Commission, Irvine: stated that the Kennedy Commission
recommends the City look at strong policies which will promote, encourage, and facilitate
housing that meets the needs of all members of the community. He encouraged the City to
look at models in other cities and to reach out to advocates and developers who know how
these developments work best.

Ezequiel Gutierrez, Public Law Center, and Greg Neville, Watermarke Properties, stated
that they would postpone their comments.

WORKSHOP

1.  Affordable Housing Discussion

  Planning Manager Elaine Lister outlined planning and zoning laws, Mission Viejo’s
  approved projects, a history of the Mejia lawsuit, and the City’s current Regional
  Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) numbers. Ms. Lister discussed the status of
  the Mission Viejo Housing Element, new legislation outlined in Senate Bill 375, the
  SCAG Envision Plan and potential development at various sites within the City.

  Celeste Brady, Community Development Agency Special Counsel, Stradling,
  Yocca, Carlson & Rauth, Newport Beach: described “of-right decrees” required by
  the State of California, density bonus laws, and statutory restrictions defined by the
  State. She outlined the limitations in housing element planning which
  redevelopment agencies are required to follow.

City Council Minutes  2  February 24, 2009
   Gail Shiomoto-Lohr, Consultant: discussed the change in direction for land use
  planning through Assembly Bill 32 and Senate Bill 375. She further discussed SB
  375’s impact on the RHNA process.

RECESS

At the hour of 7:49 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 7:59 p.m.
with four City Council Members present (Mayor Pro Tem MacLean was absent).

  Council Member Ledesma stated that the City Council should commit to building the
  required number of affordable units and should continue to stay in compliance as new
  numbers come down from the State. He expressed support for spending the $6 million
  redevelopment monies and a portion of the future allocation.

  Council Member Schlicht articulated her preference for spreading the low income housing
  units throughout the City and she stated that there is no urgency for expending the
  redevelopment funds. She further expressed an interest in giving funds to residents to
  subsidize down payments for low income housing.

  Mayor Ury stated that every city must meet the terms of State law and he supports a
  dedicated effort to stay compliant. He discussed the results of the Mejia lawsuit and noted
  the advice from legal counsel is that the City’s redevelopment monies should be put into
  play.

  Michael Keller, M.V./Dana Point: expressed concern, as a developer, that there is a lack
  of usable and available land. He encouraged the Council to pause and make sure that the
  redevelopment money is spent in the most appropriate way.

  Barbara Anderson, M.V.: stated that she appreciates what the redevelopment agency is
  trying to do but no one has mentioned the terrible state of the economy. She stated that it
  is not in the City’s best interest to buy property and there is a greater need to keep
  emergency funds and reserves available to maintain programs in troubled times.

  Special Counsel Brady noted the penalties if the redevelopment monies are not spent. The
  Community Development Agency would lose most of its discretionary ability until excess
  surplus monies are expended.

  Mark Dobrilovic, M.V.: expressed support for diversifying low-income housing and
  spreading it throughout the community.

 City Council Minutes  3  February 24, 2009
   Lin Marelic, M.V.: stated that she appreciates the comments of Council Member
  Ledesma and Council Member Schlicht and she agrees with the idea of spreading low
  income housing throughout the City so there is no marginal area of town. She further
  expressed opposition to the idea that the City would purchase land or become a landlord.

  Cesar Covarrubias, Kennedy Commission, Irvine: invited Council Members and
  members of the audience to explore low income housing in adjacent communities. He
  stated that the Kennedy Commission prides itself in educating the public on affordable
  housing projects and he recommends that the City work with non-profit developers.

  Council Member Ledesma asked how the City can protect itself and homeowners from
  potential problems when redevelopment funds are contributed to a particular project.

  Special Counsel Brady described the process for placing occupancy standards into an
  affordable housing agreement.

  Council Member Kelley noted that a large percentage of the low income units are in the
  south part of town and she supports a more even distribution of these units throughout the
  City. She attempted to dispel a rumor that the City Council Members want to build
  housing or low-income housing on top of the stores across the street from city hall.
  Council Member Kelley noted that the Council engaged a study by ULI and when they
  returned with options, one idea was to create housing at that location. She reiterated that
  the City did not act on that idea and basically said no thank you. She further stated that
  there is a scare tactic in the community regarding Council’s support for housing on the
  Casta del Sol Golf Course and she assured the public that the rumor is not true.

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she is not afraid of affordable housing and she feels
  like this Council is in panic mode when the City is in compliance. She further expressed
  support for the idea of helping homeowners with down payments.

  Special Counsel Brady stated that it is extremely difficult to use redevelopment funds this
  way and she outlined the difficulty in developing these so called “first time home buyer
  programs.”

  Roseanne Kotver, Laguna Niguel: thanked the City Council for listening to the audience
  and stated that the RHNA numbers are minimums and there is nothing wrong with a city
  going beyond the mandated number of housing units.

City Council Minutes  4  February 24, 2009
   Tina Neukirch, M.V.: stated that there is no rush to resolve these issues right now and she
  expressed support for the plan to spread affordable housing throughout the community.
  She stated that the City Council Members are the residents’ advocates and they expect the
  Council to fight for them.

  George Avila, Mission Hospital, M.V.: announced that Mission Hospital is interested in
  partnering with the City to help address this issue and to increase the number of
  affordable homes. Mr. Avila invited residents to a housing dialog event on March 10,
  2009, from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. at the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior
  Center.

  City Attorney Bill Curley provided an update on the property adjacent to Target and the
  Watermarke and UDR projects.

  Barbara Anderson, M.V.: asked for clarification on the City’s role in these projects. She
  believes that the State has put an incredible amount of restrictions on the redevelopment
  money and how it is spent.

  Marco Maquina, M.V.: speaking as a local realtor, he announced that there are 35 bank-
  owned properties in Mission Viejo and 188 homes in pre-foreclosure. He asked if the
  City has forecasted additional foreclosures on the horizon and he recommended that the
  City provide funds to help people buy these units in order to stabilize the market.

  Council Member Kelley thanked Mr. Maquina for the great idea but she noted that the
  State is asking us to build new units and will not allow the City to help buyers purchase
  homes in foreclosure.

  Council Member Ledesma asked for clarification of the density bonus statute and asked
  staff to provide a better understanding of the limitations the statute creates.

  Council Member Schlicht requested that the City develop a policy for expenditure of the
  $6 million set-aside funds so developers know what our rules are. She asked for density
  figures in writing and suggested that the City further explore subsidizing “affordable
  buyers” to some degree.

  Lin Marelic, M.V.: asked if there are any shovel-ready projects in Mission Viejo.

  Council Member Kelley clarified that we cannot build ahead for future RHNA
  allocations.

City Council Minutes  5  February 24, 2009
   Mayor Ury attempted to clarify misinformation that is circulating in the community
  regarding this Council’s work towards complying with State law. He discussed the
  City’s obligation to have an action plan and the housing-related lawsuit the City
  experienced in the past.

  Mayor Ury asked staff to provide ideas for affordable housing locations to meet the
  future RHNA allocation numbers and he invited residents to email any of the Council
  Members if questions arise after the meeting.

  City Manager Wilberg noted that the staff has updated the City’s Housing Element and
  submitted it to the State for comment. The updated Housing Element will come before
  the Council for adoption this summer. He also reminded those present that the City is
  also challenged with implementation of the regulations of SB 375.

  Council Member Ledesma commended the Mayor for facilitating this type of casual
  workshop and congratulated staff for the quick preparation. The Council must take into
  account that these issues are complicated and confusion is real, however this was a
  wonderful opportunity to share information and gain knowledge on the subject.

ADJOURNMENT

  At the hour of 9:56 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council
  at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, March 2, 2009, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 16, 2009

City Council Minutes  6  February 24, 2009
